{{Short description|Slovene chemist (1926–2021)}}
'''Miha Tišler''' (September 18, 1926 – March 25, 2021) was a [[Slovenes|Slovene]] [[chemist]] who served as a professor of chemistry at the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Technology in [[Ljubljana]], [[Slovenia]].<ref name="Stanovnik2005">{{cite journal |url=http://quod.lib.umich.edu/a/ark/5550190.0002.501?rgn=main;view=fulltext |title=A Tribute to Prof. Miha Tišler |first=Branko |last=Stanovnik |authorlink=Branko Stanovnik |date=June 26, 2005 |journal=Arkivoc |volume=2001 |issue=5 |pages=1–6 |doi=10.3998/ark.5550190.0002.501|doi-access=free |hdl=2027/spo.5550190.0002.501 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sazu.si/events/605f095412416e9924e4eac9 |title=Umrl akad. Miha Tišler |publisher=[[Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts]] |accessdate=March 29, 2021}}</ref>

Tišler was the author of 50 books and monographs on [[heterocyclic chemistry]], and he was named a [[Order of St. Gregory the Great|Knight of the Order of St. Gregory the Great]].<ref name="Stanovnik2005"/>

Miha Tišler was born in Ljubljana on September 18, 1926. In 1955 he was appointed a professor of chemistry at the University of Ljubljana. In 1977 he received the Kidrič Prize. From 1978 to 1980 he served as the president of International Society of Heterocyclic Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.delo.si/znanje/znanost/akademik-dr-miha-tisler-devetdesetletnik.html|title=Akademik dr. Miha Tišler, devetdesetletnik|work=Delo|date=13 October 2016}}</ref>
